WITH per_order_avgs AS (
  SELECT 
    ordersmark,
    AVG(fillcount) as per_order_avg
  FROM orderexecutions
  GROUP BY ordersmark
),
first_benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(per_order_avg) as benchmark
  FROM per_order_avgs
),
above_first AS (
  SELECT poa.per_order_avg
  FROM per_order_avgs poa
  CROSS JOIN first_benchmark fb
  WHERE poa.per_order_avg > fb.benchmark
),
second_benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(per_order_avg) as benchmark
  FROM above_first
),
final_orders AS (
  SELECT 
    af.per_order_avg,
    af.per_order_avg - fb.benchmark as first_excess,
    af.per_order_avg - sb.benchmark as second_excess
  FROM above_first af
  CROSS JOIN first_benchmark fb
  CROSS JOIN second_benchmark sb
  WHERE af.per_order_avg > sb.benchmark
)
SELECT 
  AVG(per_order_avg) as avg_per_order_fill_qty,
  AVG(first_excess) as avg_first_excess,
  AVG(second_excess) as avg_second_excess
FROM final_orders

assumptions.assumption: Ignoring missing quantities means NULL values in fillcount are excluded from AVG calculations (standard SQL behavior), while zero-quantity executions are counted as 0
Executions with NULL ordersmark are grouped together as a single distinct group for aggregation purposes
Keeping orders above a benchmark uses strict inequality (>), not (>=), excluding orders equal to the benchmark
